method: Same selection system as live play: random subjects and formats, then random unseen questions. Recent subjects are avoided to keep the mix varied; first 100.

questions.prompt: Name a Legendary or Mythical Pokémon.
questions.scope: Species classified as Legendary or Mythical in the pinned PokéAPI data count. Forms share their species' answer identity. Pseudo-Legendary is a fan label and does not make a species Legendary.

questions.prompt: Name an animal people have used for work or transport.
questions.scope: Documented domesticated or trained working animals count, past or present.

questions.prompt: Name a country made up entirely of islands.
questions.scope: Island countries and countries sharing an island count; Australia explicitly counts.

questions.prompt: Name a song by SZA.
questions.scope: Released recordings credited to SZA count, including collaborations, features and released covers. Writing or production credit alone does not count. Different versions share one answer.

questions.prompt: Name a type of headwear or head covering.
questions.scope: Real kinds of hat, cap, helmet or other wearable head covering count, including religious and historical headwear. Fictional magical items and names of individual objects do not.

questions.prompt: Name an anime TV or streaming show.
Name a type of ball used in a sport, game or athletic training.
questions.scope: Named balls used in sports, games or athletic training count, including particular game-ball designs. Pucks, shuttlecocks and punching bags are not balls.

questions.prompt: Name a flower or flowering block found in Minecraft.
questions.scope: Flower items and blocks count, including tall flowers and Nether-compatible flowers. Named crops and saplings do not become flowers merely because they are plants. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

questions.prompt: Name a food crop with an edible part that normally grows underground.
questions.scope: Roots, tubers, rhizomes, bulbs, corms and underground fruits count. Named crop kinds and established edible varieties count. A normal above-ground fruit does not count merely because the plant has roots.

questions.prompt: Name a structure or component found in a living cell.
questions.scope: Plant, animal, fungal and prokaryotic cell structures count. Whole organs or tissues are not structures inside one cell. Established molecular structures such as DNA and chromosomes count. Cellular structures and molecular assemblies count; an individual pigment such as chlorophyll is not an organelle or cell structure by itself.

questions.prompt: Name a musical instrument with a keyboard.
questions.scope: Recognized keyboard-instrument types and documented named keyboard instruments or models count. Keys and buttons form the musical playing interface; having ordinary valves or attaching an external controller does not automatically qualify another instrument.

questions.prompt: Name an object that commonly has a hinge.
questions.scope: A common hinged version of the object must exist. Sliding or roll-up versions do not prevent a genuinely hinged object from counting.

questions.prompt: Name a fictional animal character.
questions.scope: Named animal characters from any published story count; real celebrity pets do not.

questions.prompt: Name an exercise that can be done using your bodyweight instead of added weights.
questions.scope: Named exercises and recognized variations count, including floor exercises, holds and movements on a pull-up bar. A bar or bench can provide support; dumbbells and loaded barbells are not required.

questions.prompt: Name a government-issued currency, monetary unit or named historical coin.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name an ice-cream topping or mix-in.
questions.scope: Named toppings and mix-ins used on ice cream, gelato or frozen custard count, including candy, fruit, nuts, sauces and cake pieces. A flavor by itself is not a topping.

questions.prompt: Name a type of tree.
Name a tool, instrument or piece of glassware used in a science laboratory.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name an artist associated with pop music.
Name a type of paint.
questions.scope: Types of paint defined by medium, finish or purpose count, including artist and building paints. Color names alone, a layer of paint and digital painting software do not.

questions.prompt: Name a professional sports team whose name includes an animal.
questions.scope: The team nickname must name an animal or animal group. A city name alone, such as Buffalo, does not count.

questions.prompt: Name a type of exercise.
Name a recognized pizza style or named pizza variety.
questions.scope: Recognized regional styles and named pizza varieties count. A topping by itself is not a pizza style, and an invented topping combination is not a new variety.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of animal that can pollinate flowers.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a cloud type, form or recognized cloud feature.
questions.scope: Cloud genera, species, varieties and recognized cloud features count, along with established common names such as lenticular cloud, contrail and fog at ground level. Weather events, precipitation and a blue sky alone do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a landform, natural feature or kind of landscape.
Name a character from the Harry Potter books or films.
questions.scope: Identifiable characters in the Harry Potter novels, films and their epilogues count, including creatures, ghosts and portraits. Real actors are not their fictional characters. Same-name characters share one answer identity.

questions.prompt: Name a sport or competitive game.
Name a piece of camping equipment.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a game on Steam tagged “Racing”.
Name a kind of wild cat.
questions.scope: Living and recently extinct species in the Mammal Diversity Database, plus established named animal groups, count. English names, documented scientific names and genuine public synonyms count. Prehistoric fossil-only species are outside this current-species inventory. Domestic cat breeds and captive cross-species hybrids do not count. Named tiger and lion populations share their parent species identity.

questions.prompt: Name a three-dimensional geometric shape.
questions.scope: Established types and named examples count. Alternate standard names are the same answer.

questions.prompt: Name a food that is commonly pickled.
questions.scope: Vegetables, fruits, eggs, meats and seafood with established pickled preparations count. Vinegar and brine are ingredients, not foods being pickled.

questions.prompt: Name a music festival.
questions.scope: Named public music festivals anywhere in the world count; a one-off concert does not.

questions.prompt: Name a real named canal.
questions.scope: Named canals, shipping channels and recognized artificial waterways count worldwide, including disused historical ones. Natural rivers are not automatically canals.

questions.prompt: Name an animation movie.
Name a champion in League of Legends.
questions.scope: Base-game and recorded expansion names count. Versions of the same named object count once.

questions.prompt: Name a water sport or recreational activity on or in water.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name an animal that can produce its own light.
questions.scope: Bioluminescence, including light produced by symbiotic bacteria in an animal's light organ, counts. Reflection, fluorescence and bright coloring alone do not. Broad animal groups count when they contain documented luminous members.

questions.prompt: Name something people open using a key or a code.
questions.scope: Physical objects and devices count; the code can be a password or combination.

questions.prompt: Name a guitar manufacturer or established guitar brand, including historical makers.
questions.scope: Types, named examples and established synonyms count. This is a finite source inventory.

questions.prompt: Name a piece of equipment used to take or process photographs.
questions.scope: Physical equipment, supplies and accessories used in still photography count, including darkroom materials. A finished photograph, filmed sequence or a device used only to mark a film take does not.

questions.prompt: Name a type of tower.
questions.scope: Types of built tower count, including towers defined by their function or structure. Individual named towers do not.

questions.prompt: Name a fictional pirate.
questions.scope: Named fictional sea, air and space pirates count, including characters who were pirates earlier in their story. A smuggler, sailor or marine is not automatically a pirate.

questions.prompt: Name a driver who has competed in Formula One.
questions.scope: Drivers in the complete Jolpica/Ergast Formula One World Championship driver inventory count, including historical entrants and the Indianapolis 500 when it was part of that championship. A real surname can identify a valid driver; invented initials and racing three-letter codes do not count as names.

questions.prompt: Name a food commonly served on a stick.
questions.scope: Named foods and established skewer dishes count, including sweets.

questions.prompt: Name an animal that changes color.
questions.scope: Rapid camouflage and seasonal changes both count.

questions.prompt: Name an item that restores health in a video game.
questions.scope: Named consumables, pickups and healing items count; name the actual item.

questions.prompt: Name a song with a person's name in its title.
questions.scope: Released songs count; the name can be a real person or a fictional person.

questions.prompt: Name one of the 88 official constellations.
questions.scope: Official IAU constellation names count. Recognized common names such as Capricorn and the Great Bear are accepted. Asterisms such as the Big Dipper are only parts of constellations.

questions.prompt: Name a horror movie.
Name a spoken, signed or constructed language.
Name a named dish or preparation in which eggs are a main ingredient.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a player who has won the NBA regular-season MVP award.
questions.scope: Winners of the main NBA regular-season Most Valuable Player award through the 2025–26 season count. Finals, All-Star and other leagues' MVP awards are different.

questions.prompt: Name an item or product used to wash, dry or care for laundry.
questions.scope: Laundry appliances, supplies, stain treatments and clothes-care tools count, as do named product types and established laundry-product brands, including historical ones. A garment itself is not a laundry supply.

questions.prompt: Name a song by Coldplay.
questions.scope: Released recordings credited to Coldplay count, including collaborations, features and released covers. Writing or production credit alone does not count. Different versions share one answer.

questions.prompt: Name a body part a typical human has more than one of.
questions.scope: Named bones, organs and body parts count; ordinary singular names would be accepted.

questions.prompt: Name a film actor or actress.
Name a kind of animal that can regrow a lost body part.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a type of boat, ship or other watercraft.
questions.scope: Kinds of boat, ship, raft or other vessel designed to travel on water or underwater count, past or present. Individual named vessels, wrecks, ice-only vehicles and descriptors of condition alone do not.

questions.prompt: Name a named salad or established salad variety.
questions.scope: Types, named examples and established synonyms count. This is a finite source inventory.

questions.prompt: Name a player who has played for the Detroit Pistons.
questions.scope: At least one first-team NBA, BAA or ABA game for this franchise counts, past or present. Coaches, draft rights and preseason-only appearances do not. NBA/BAA seasons as the Fort Wayne Pistons also count.

questions.prompt: Name a game on Steam tagged “Action”.
Name a musician known for playing drums.
questions.scope: Real musicians known for playing drums count, including multi-instrumentalists and percussionists with a documented drum-playing career. An unrelated band member does not become a drummer just because the band has one.

questions.prompt: Name a web browser.
questions.scope: Actual web-browser products and families count, including historical, mobile and text browsers. A search engine, rendering engine, extension, website or operating system alone is not a browser.

questions.prompt: Name a tool or piece of equipment used for gardening.
questions.scope: Tools, devices and durable equipment used to plant, water, prune, move soil or maintain gardens count. Plant names are not tools.

questions.prompt: Name a fictional detective.
questions.scope: Named fictional professional detectives and amateur sleuths count across books, comics, film, TV and games. A character must actually investigate cases; merely appearing in a mystery does not qualify.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of parrot.
questions.scope: Parrot species and established named groups count, including recently extinct species in the source taxonomy. Common and scientific names count. Pet colour mutations share their species identity; a bird is not a parrot just because its name contains that word.

questions.prompt: Name a player who has played for the Sacramento Kings.
questions.scope: At least one first-team NBA, BAA or ABA game for this franchise counts, past or present. Coaches, draft rights and preseason-only appearances do not. Rochester Royals, Cincinnati Royals, Kansas City-Omaha Kings and Kansas City Kings seasons also count.

questions.prompt: Name a country whose national flag contains a star.
questions.scope: A visible star on the official national flag qualifies; tiny stars inside a coat of arms count too.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of flatbread.
questions.scope: Recognized flatbread types, named regional breads and flatbread dishes count, including leavened and unleavened types. Ordinary sandwich loaves, toppings and ingredients alone do not count.

questions.prompt: Name an artist associated with rock music.
Name a unit used to measure a physical quantity or digital information.
questions.scope: Established metric, customary, historical and scientific measurement units count, including named prefixed units. Currency units and arbitrary made-up units do not. Official unit symbols are accepted only when they name that actual unit.

questions.prompt: Name a mystery TV or streaming show.
Name a bird of prey.
questions.scope: Established types and named examples count. Alternate standard names are the same answer.

questions.prompt: Name a motorsport or established motor-racing series.
questions.scope: Recognized motor-vehicle competitions and racing series count, including cars, motorcycles, boats, snowmobiles and powered aircraft. Drivers, vehicle manufacturers and unpowered sports do not qualify by themselves.

questions.prompt: Name a type of footwear.
Name a snack food or established named snack. Brands of specific snacks count.
Name an item or block a furnace recipe can produce in Minecraft.
questions.scope: Give the output, rather than the input, of an ordinary furnace smelting or cooking recipe. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

questions.prompt: Name a real valley, canyon or gorge.
questions.scope: Real named valleys, canyons and gorges on Earth count. Features conventionally known by these names count, including Bryce Canyon. Fictional places and a whole country alone do not count.

questions.prompt: Name an animated TV series.
questions.scope: Shows for any audience count, including cartoons, anime and streaming series.

questions.prompt: Name a human muscle or muscle group.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a player who has been on an NFL or AFL roster (1920–2026).
Name a dance style, traditional dance, or named social dance.
Name something that can be controlled with a remote.
questions.scope: A real consumer product type with a handheld or app-based remote qualifies.

questions.prompt: Name a type of custard or a dessert made with custard.
questions.scope: Named custards and desserts made using custard or custard powder count. A cream-only filling does not qualify merely because it is called cream.

questions.prompt: Name a landlocked country.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a fantasy movie.
Name a kind of animal in the weasel family.
questions.scope: Living and recently extinct species in the Mammal Diversity Database, plus established named animal groups, count. English names, documented scientific names and genuine public synonyms count. Prehistoric fossil-only species are outside this current-species inventory.

questions.prompt: Name a sport played with a racket, bat, stick or club.
questions.scope: Any one of those implements qualifies; named sport variants count.

questions.prompt: Name an invention, tool or piece of technology.
Name a playable fighter in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.
questions.scope: All base-game, Echo and DLC fighters count. Pokémon Trainer's three Pokémon, the three Mii fighting styles, and Pyra/Mythra count separately. Alternate costumes share the original fighter's answer; Assist Trophies do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a song by The Beatles.
questions.scope: Released recordings credited to The Beatles count, including collaborations, features and released covers. Writing or production credit alone does not count. Different versions share one answer.

questions.prompt: Name a named dish commonly made with chicken.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of box or boxed storage container.
questions.scope: Types of physical box, chest, crate and boxed storage container count, including cases with a recognizable box form. Metaphorical boxes and software do not.

questions.prompt: Name a comedy movie.
Name an animal that makes a regular seasonal migration.
questions.scope: Named species and animal groups with documented recurring seasonal, breeding or feeding migrations count, including migrating populations of a species. One-off escapes or an individual simply wandering do not.

questions.prompt: Name a real mountain, mountain peak or volcano.
questions.scope: Named mountains, mountain peaks and volcanoes on Earth count. Whole mountain ranges, unnamed coordinates, fictional mountains and names only found on other planets are outside this inventory.

questions.prompt: Name a type of lamp or lighting fixture.
questions.scope: Real lamps, lighting fixtures and manufactured light sources count, including candles and historical lighting. Fictional individual lamps, stars and naturally glowing organisms do not.

questions.prompt: Name a sport or recognized sporting discipline played on snow or ice.
questions.scope: Established ice and snow sports and competitive disciplines count. A sport merely played during the winter on an ordinary indoor court does not qualify.
